title: Customer Claim Exchange and SIG/CAIQ Compact Generator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Enable a compact, machine-readable exchange format for customer security claims plus a SIG/CAIQ compact generator that auto-populates standard questionnaire answers. Goal: reduce time-to-response for enterprise RFPs and enable a priced credit/claim model that can be purchased by customers to accelerate procurement. This work sits at the intersection of product, legal, and solutions engineering and will include a UX for curated claim packages, signed assertions, and a lightweight CAIQ export that maps to common controls.
acceptance_criteria: Compact claim exchange API v1 published with schema definition and example payloads
SIG/CAIQ compact generator available in Console with preview and export (JSON/ZIP)
Customer can purchase claim-credit bundles and redeem them to auto-generate an evidence pack
Telemetry: time-to-first-response and reduction in manual effort measured via support tags
Security review completed and signed-off by Security & Legal
success_metrics: Reduce median questionnaire response time from 7 days to <= 2 days for pilot customers
Achieve 20% conversion of engaged trials to paid claim-credit bundles within 30 days
Decrease engineering time spent on ad-hoc CAIQ requests by 50% across pilot accounts
comments_and_updates: 2025-02-20: Kickoff meeting with PM, Solutions Eng, Legal, Security. Agreed scope: compact generator (CAIQ-lite) + claim exchange API + pricing experiment. Action: Solutions Eng to draft schema.

2025-02-24: First draft of compact schema uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/compact-schema-v0.1. Noted open question: signed assertions format (JWT vs separate signature file).

2025-02-27: Engineering spike finished. ENG-84210 prototype demonstrates export pipeline and zip bundle structure. Spike notes: prefer detached signatures (RFC7515) for verifiability across buyer systems. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/pull/7261

2025-03-01: Pricing experiment proposal reviewed with Growth. Proposed two levers: pay-per-claim-credit ($X/claim) + monthly unlimited tier for large enterprises. Growth requested simulated revenue model (see sheet).

2025-03-03: Design mockups for Console flows reviewed. Key feedback from UX: make default export human-readable summary + machine JSON. Mockups: https://www.figma.com/file/fake/compact-generator-mockups

2025-03-04: Security review kickoff scheduled. Legal requested retention and audit-log controls in first release; added as must-have. Blockers: SSO-scoped access controls for claim redaction (ENG-85120).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: Fully templated CAIQ answers vs. curated claim packages. Chosen approach: curated claim packages that map to CAIQ-lite, enabling human review before final export.
Potential integration partners: Solutions Engineering teams at top-10 enterprise pilots for early buy-in.
Fallback plan: if signed assertions integration delays, ship unsigned compact export with audit trail and a visible "attestation pending" flag.
Linked artifacts: Confluence spec (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Compact+Claim+Exchange+Spec), pricing spreadsheet, pilot contact list (Drive).
next_steps: Finalize compact claim schema (owner: Marco Li) by 2025-03-07
Complete Security review for signature model and retention by 2025-03-10
Build Console export UI MVP and payment flow stub (ENG-85120) during Cycle 2025-W10
Recruit 3 pilot customers and schedule onboarding sessions by 2025-03-21
